plot.label: Graph of a sinusoidal function f for t from 0 to 12: highest points (0, 1), (6, 1) and (12, 1), lowest points (3, -3) and (9, -3)

sinusoidal-functions-s2.title: A buoy on the waves
sinusoidal-functions-s2.text: A buoy bobs up and down. Its height above the sea floor is a sinusoidal function of time, and its greatest and least heights appear in the table.

table.caption: Height $h(t)$ of the buoy above the sea floor, in meters, $t$ seconds after a stopwatch starts

why.correct: The greatest value is $1$ and the least is $-3$: amplitude $= \frac{1 - (-3)}{2} = 2$.
options: $4$ is the full distance from the lowest to the highest point, twice the amplitude.
$1$ is the greatest value, measured from the $t$-axis instead of from the midline.
$3$ is the size of the least value, measured from the $t$-axis instead of from the midline.

items.q: What is the midline of the graph of $f$?

why.correct: The midline is halfway between $1$ and $-3$: $y = \frac{1 + (-3)}{2} = -1$.
options: Average of the greatest and least values.
The $t$-axis is not the midline here: the wave reaches 1 above it but 3 below it.
$-3$ is the least value, the bottom of the wave, not its center line.
$2$ is the amplitude, not the height of the midline.

mistakes.why: That is from a highest point to the next lowest point, half a cycle. Measure from $(0, 1)$ to the next highest point $(6, 1)$.
The window shows two full cycles. One cycle runs from $t = 0$ to $t = 6$.

why.correct: Highest points at $t = 0$ and $t = 6$: one full cycle takes 6 units.

items.q: What is the frequency of $f$, in cycles per unit of $t$?

mistakes.why: That is the period. Frequency is its reciprocal: $\frac{1}{6}$ of a cycle per unit.
Two cycles appear in the window, but the window is 12 units wide: $\frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}$ cycle per unit.

items.q: What is the average rate of change of $f$ on $[0, 3]$?

why.correct: $\frac{f(3) - f(0)}{3 - 0} = \frac{-3 - 1}{3} = -\frac{4}{3}$, the slope of the secant line through $(0, 1)$ and $(3, -3)$.
options: Change in output $-4$ over change in input $3$.
$-4$ is the change in output; divide by the 3 units of input.
This is the change in input over the change in output, upside down.
This uses the amplitude 2 as the change in output; the graph drops 4, from the top to the bottom.

items.q: What is the amplitude of $h$, in meters?

mistakes.why: That is $\max - \min$, the full swing. The amplitude is half of it.
That is the midline height. The amplitude is how far the buoy goes above or below it.

why.correct: The greatest height 3.8 m occurs at $t = 2$ and next at $t = 10$: one cycle takes 8 seconds.
options: $h(0) = h(4) = 3$, but at $t = 0$ the buoy is rising and at $t = 4$ it is falling: only half a cycle.
This is the spacing of the table, a quarter of a cycle.
This is the length of the whole table, a cycle and a half.

items.q: What is the frequency of the buoy's motion, in cycles per second?

mistakes.why: That is the period in seconds per cycle. The frequency is its reciprocal.
That uses 4 seconds as the period, but $t = 0$ to $t = 4$ is only half a cycle.

why.correct: The period is 8 seconds, so the frequency is $\frac{1}{8} = 0.125$ cycle per second.

items.q: If the pattern continues, what is the buoy's height at $t = 18$ seconds, in meters?

mistakes.why: That is $h(16) = h(0)$. Two periods take you to $t = 16$; two more seconds give $h(2)$.

items.q: What are the amplitude and midline of $y = 4\sin\theta + 1$?

why.correct: $4\sin\theta$ goes from $-4$ to $4$; adding 1 gives $-3$ to $5$. Amplitude $\frac{5 - (-3)}{2} = 4$, midline $y = \frac{5 + (-3)}{2} = 1$.
options: The factor 4 sets the amplitude; the added 1 sets the midline.
The roles are swapped: 4 multiplies the heights, 1 lifts them.
5 is the greatest value, not the amplitude, and the graph is lifted off $y = 0$.

items.q: For a number $k$, $\sin k = 0.3$. What is $\sin(-k)$?

mistakes.why: Sine is odd: reflecting the angle across the $x$-axis flips the height, so $\sin(-k) = -\sin k$.
That is $1 - 0.3$. Sine is odd, so $\sin(-k) = -0.3$.

why.correct: The point at angle $-k$ is the point at $k$ reflected across the $x$-axis, so its height changes sign: $\sin(-k) = -0.3$.

items.q: A guitar string vibrates with a frequency of 220 cycles per second. What is the period of its vibration, in seconds?

mistakes.why: That is the frequency, in cycles per second. The period, seconds per cycle, is its reciprocal.
$2\pi$ is the period of $\sin\theta$, but here the period is just the time for one cycle: $\frac{1}{220}$ second.

items.q: A pendulum's horizontal position, measured from a mark on the floor, swings smoothly between $-12$ cm and $18$ cm. Its position is a sinusoidal function of time. What are its amplitude and midline?

why.correct: Amplitude $\frac{18 - (-12)}{2} = 15$ cm; midline $x = \frac{18 + (-12)}{2} = 3$. Check: $3 \pm 15$ gives $18$ and $-12$.
options: Half the swing, and the average of the two extremes.
30 cm is the whole swing, twice the amplitude.
The mark on the floor is not the center of the swing: the pendulum goes further right than left.
18 is the greatest position, not the amplitude, and $\frac{18 - 12}{2} = 3$, not 6.

items.q: Which functions are sinusoidal? Select all that apply.

why.correct: Both are the sine wave after dilations and translations: cosine is sine shifted, and the 3, $-2$ and $+5$ stretch and lift it.
options: A cosine graph stretched by 3 and moved down 2.
An exponential function keeps growing; it never repeats.

items.q: A sinusoidal function has greatest value 10 and least value 2. The greatest value is changed to 14; the least value and the cycle length stay the same. Predict each change.

variables.name: The amplitude
variables.why: The swing grows from $10 - 2 = 8$ to $14 - 2 = 12$, so the amplitude goes from 4 to 6.

variables.name: The period
variables.why: The heights change, but each cycle still takes the same length of input.

why.correct: Raising only the top stretches the wave and lifts its center line; the cycle length is separate.

items.q: Which statement is true for every number $\theta$?

why.correct: The angles $\theta$ and $-\theta$ give points that are reflections across the $x$-axis: same $x$-coordinate, so cosine is even.
options: False at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$: $\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1$, not 1. Sine is odd.
